keyVerseText: And say thou unto the people, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh: for ye have wept in the ears of the LORD, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for it was well with us in Egypt: therefore the LORD will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew root טוֹב (ṭôwb) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the sense of goodness and pleasantness. Beyond the simple English gloss of 'good,' the root carries a rich semantic field including notions of delight, benefit, and well-being. This breadth indicates that the word encompasses not only moral goodness but also experiential and relational goodness, such as joy, favor, and health.
usageInScripture: With 25 occurrences, טוֹב (ṭôwb) appears consistently in contexts expressing positive states or actions. The top translations, including 'If it please,' 'thou didst well,' and 'If it seem good,' reveal its frequent use in expressing approval, satisfaction, or beneficial outcomes. This range from describing what is pleasing to what is beneficial or right shows the word's versatility in capturing both subjective delight and objective goodness.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding טוֹב (ṭôwb) enriches our grasp of God's nature and His dealings with humanity, as it highlights the goodness that is intrinsic to God’s character and His will. The word’s scope—from joy and delight to right action—reflects the holistic goodness God desires for His people, encompassing moral righteousness and the flourishing of life. In Christ, this goodness is perfectly embodied and extended to believers, inviting them to live in a way that is pleasing and beneficial to God and others. Recognizing טוֹב as both an attribute and an action helps believers appreciate the fullness of God’s good will and their call to reflect that goodness in daily life.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 11:18 states, 'for it was well with us in Egypt,' using טוֹב to express a state of well-being and satisfaction that the people longed for. Here, טוֹב conveys more than mere preference; it signifies a condition of blessing and contentment that the Israelites remembered. This usage underscores the word’s role in describing favorable circumstances and God’s provision, reminding believers that true goodness comes from God’s care and the fulfillment of His promises.
